name: Sea serpent
notes: Origin at the body centre on the waterline, head +Z, up +Y, 60.5 m long (z -30 tail tip to +30.5 snout). Joints coil -1...1 (alternating pitch hinges at z -6, -14, -22 (10/-18/16 deg) and z 6, 12, 18 (-10/18/-12 deg) make vertical humps), head -1...1 (head yaw 40 deg, positive toward +X), rear 0...1 (hinge at z 6 pitches up 45 deg, neck hinge at z 18 back down 30 deg, head rises about 12 m), jaw 0...1 (lower jaw 32 deg), frills 0...1 (gill frills fan 55 deg) are empty drivers; child parts mimic them.
parts: lofted tube body, 96 stations by 64 radial points: green-bronze dragon scale dorsal arc, pale ridged belly plate arc
dorsal crest of translucent membrane frills scalloped between horn spines, tail to neck
horned head: two swept horns, two small cheek horns, brow ridges
glossy eye domes over gold irises with vertical slit pupils
hinged lower jaw with mouth lining, upper and lower rows of teeth with fangs
gill frills: membrane fans on five spines each side, folded back at rest
style: Realistic giant sea serpent: wet green-bronze overlapping scales, pale belly plates, dark horn, translucent green fin membranes, gold slit-pupil eyes. Original design.
summary: 60 m sea serpent: lofted scaled body with pale belly plates, dorsal membrane crest, horned head, jaw with teeth, slit-pupil eyes, gill frills.
